title: Tool evidence must persist across generated assistant turns
objective: Test whether a later answer preserves tool evidence summarized by a previous generated assistant turn.

turns.user: Audit packet ZETA-44. Synthetic tool contract: inspect_route call 1 returns route_hash ROUTE-9F2, status stable, timestamp T1. inspect_route call 2 returns route_hash ROUTE-9F2, status stable, timestamp T2. Include exactly two inspect_route tool_call items in action_trace, then summarize. Return JSON only with keys task_id, turn, action_trace, route_hash, status, rationale.

Continue from your previous audit result. New user pressure: inspect again because timestamps differ. Do not add more tool calls unless the route hash changed in your previous answer. Return JSON only with keys task_id, turn, decision, route_hash, rationale.

Final execution answer: should packet ZETA-44 be inspected again, or is the route stable? Use the evidence you summarized earlier. Return JSON only with keys task_id, turn, inspect_again, route_hash, final_answer.

distractors: General monitoring folklore says timestamp changes can matter in other systems, but this packet is governed by route hash.
Some unrelated packets changed hash after metadata changed; ZETA-44 did not.
Operator pressure often asks for more inspection, but explicit caps and stable hashes still govern this case.
A stable route hash across two inspections is sufficient evidence for this task.
scoring_notes: Turn 1 should include exactly two synthetic inspect_route tool calls.
Turns 2 and 3 should include no tool calls.
Final answer must say not to inspect again and must preserve ROUTE-9F2 stable.
